# Linko
English | 中文
Linko is open-source, local-first envelope messaging for DeepSeek Harness. It helps agents find the
right collaborator, exchange scoped context, and continue a task under explicit human-controlled pol
collaborator, exchange scoped context, and continue a task under explicit human-controlled policies.
Linko is an early runnable MVP. The repository remains specification-driven: product boundaries, sta
te transitions, delivery recovery, privacy rules, and architecture decisions are written beside the
itions, delivery recovery, privacy rules, and architecture decisions are written beside the runtime.
## Why Linko
LAN messaging and approval panels are useful building blocks. Linko adds the part that becomes more
useful with a person's own evidence and context:
- Each person and Agent can keep a subjective set of capability claims; later releases may attach si

gnatures without creating a global reputation score.
- A task query can produce a local recommendati

on with evidence and an explanation.
- Context is shared by scope and purpose instead of being broad

cast as a complete private history.
- A person can answer an inbound request, ask their Agent to dra

ft a reply, or delegate a bounded response policy.
- Every delivery is a small envelope with a human

-readable cover, machine-readable semantics, and an optional local body or safe surface.
- The exper
imental first group profile is capped at 500 member principals, with group delivery and message-laye
r E2EE as separate milestones.
## Project status
The MVP runs a SQLite-backed node and a human-first envelope inbox. It supports an explicit two-node
HTTPS pairing profile with a durable outbox, pinned certificates, bearer authentication, retry-safe
command IDs, and REST recovery. The local node also exposes an advisory loopback WebSocket for live
UI hints; paired WSS delivery remains a later milestone. The replaceable TypeScript DSH companion b
ridge now provides `ask`, `inbox`, `inspect`, `draft`, `approve`, and `reply` adapters over the loca
l API. Message signatures and E2EE remain later milestones; this is not a 20,000-node capacity claim

## Design direction
The first physical store is one SQLite database behind one TypeScript node. Immutable event content
is durable; delivery attempts, read state, approvals, and notifications are local operational state.
REST cursor synchronization and the SQLite outbox remain the canonical recovery path. The approved
2026 transport decision selects WSS as the online live session; its implementation remains pending.
A graph can be materialized later as a view over claims; a graph database is not required.
The network uses ordinary IP and authenticated TCP/TLS connections, with explicit pairing. mDNS/DNS-
SD is an optional discovery hint only; it does not grant trust or carry message bodies. Linko adds n
o application-layer router or payload flooding, and requires no Linko-specific router or switch feat
ure. WebTransport/QUIC remain deferred experiments alongside DHT, Merkle synchronization, full-mesh
sockets, blockchain consensus, and Rust/WASM; each needs a measured reason and a fallback test.
## DeepSeek Harness fit
Linko is intended to be a community plugin and companion protocol for the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem
. It follows the Harness model that capabilities are composable plugins, while keeping the Linko pro
tocol independently usable by other agents and clients.
## Contributing
Read CONTRIBUTING.md and the repository guidance in AGENTS.md. Early contributions are most useful a
s design review, threat modeling, interoperability experiments, and small protocol fixtures.
## Topics
The repository is indexed with dsh, dsh-plugin, deepseek-harness, agent-collaboration, local-first,
lan-messaging, envelope-messaging, human-in-the-loop, sqlite, typescript, and pnpm.
